principle: Each amendment is recorded before the endpoint it affects is evaluated. None changes a batch1 result or a claim grade.

amendments.kind: source code observation and added diagnostic implementation
amendments.observation: In sim_two_pop_model.m (archive SHA-256 404697263ca941b1b74dee9feb4c4680ff3077d9e20bb7105482d17f14e96a70, member identical to live Git blob 9cf4e967cd19f17b968ff175d129529ac5f40312), the branch that selects the slow-population loss event compares the uniform draw against a cumulative sum whose last two terms are the same variable: (wf1+wf2+ws2+ws2)/w in function_2_population_model and (ws1+ws2+wp2+wp2)/w in function_2_population_model_ageing. The intended cumulative sum is the total propensity w. When the slow-population renewal probability q equals 0.5 the two expressions coincide and nothing changes. When q differs from 0.5 the loss interval is empty (q greater than 0.5) or a draw can fall past the last branch and advance time without any event (both cases).
amendments.consequence_to_test: The Red2Kras RFP parameter block uses r = q = 0.7 before and after tau, so in a source-literal run the slow population never loses a cell and its effective dynamics become pure birth at rate q*sigma rather than birth q*sigma and death (1-q)*sigma. The Confetti and Red2Kras YFP blocks use r = q = 0.5 and are unaffected. Numerical size of the effect on the n>=2 clone-size distribution has not been calculated at freeze time.
amendments.implementation_change: Add a third implementation, 'source-literal with corrected branch cumulative', to the two already frozen (source-literal; boundary-correct Gillespie). It reproduces every other literal behaviour (event applied after the horizon is crossed, old rate across the tau boundary, founder allocation rep <= fraction*nclones counted from zero) and changes only the branch cumulative to the total propensity. Its purpose is to attribute any literal-versus-corrected difference to the branch typo separately from the horizon and rate-switch behaviours.
amendments.interpretation_boundary: This is a code observation about the deposited script. It does not show which implementation produced the published best-fit curves, and it does not by itself change any published parameter or claim.

amendments.observation: The contract specifies igraph Louvain. No 'louvain' Python package is installed in the verified runtime. igraph 1.0.0 exposes Graph.community_multilevel(weights, return_levels, resolution), which is the Louvain multilevel algorithm with a resolution parameter.
amendments.implementation_change: Louvain is run through igraph community_multilevel with the contract resolutions 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5 and seed 20260928 set through igraph's random generator. This satisfies the frozen algorithm; it is not Leiden and is not an exact reproduction of Seurat's Louvain implementation.

amendments.observation: The primary inclusion rule removes automatic doublets. Batch1 already ran scanpy Scrublet (seed 20260927) on every library, and its per-cell flags are cached with barcodes under processed/batch1/rna.
amendments.implementation_change: Continuation scripts may join batch1 doublet flags by barcode after asserting that the source-QC cell set is identical, instead of rerunning Scrublet. Module scores are never inherited from batch1 caches; they are recomputed from counts with the mapped-gene denominator as the handoff requires.

missing: scrublet standalone package (scanpy's built-in Scrublet is available)
